"""Single merged catalog of the image library.

The UI used to hold four independent feeds (provider catalog, saved computers
and the custom coworking gallery) with three different item shapes.  This
module flattens them into ONE list of :class:`CatalogImage` so a single grid can
render, search and filter the whole library with one request.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Any, Dict, Iterable, List, Optional
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

SOURCE_PROVIDER = "provider" -- no, source values are provider names.

class CatalogImage(BaseModel):
    source: str = Field(description="linuxserver, kasmweb, browseruse, custom or saved")
    id: str
    name: str
    description: Optional[str] = None
    type: Optional[str] = Field(default=None, description="UI type: desktop, application, browser, saved, custom")
    tags: List[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    visibility: Optional[str] = None
    status: str = "ready"
    icon_url: Optional[str] = None
    preview_url: Optional[str] = None
    has_preview_blob: bool = False
    image: Optional[str] = None
    provider: Optional[str] = None
    coworking_image: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None


class CatalogImageListResponse(BaseModel):
    count: int
    images: List[CatalogImage]


def _provider_items(images) -> List[CatalogImage]:
    items = []
    for image in images or []:
        items.append(CatalogImage(
            source=getattr(image, "provider", "") or "curated",
            id=image.id,
            name=image.name,
            description=image.description or None,
            type=_provider_type(image),
            tags=list(image.tags or []),
            visibility="global",
            status="ready",
            icon_url=image.icon_url,
            preview_url=image.screenshot_url,
            has_preview_blob=False,
            image=image.image,
            provider=image.provider,
        ))
    return items
```

    kasm = list_images(provider="kasmweb")

    assert linuxserver and all(image.provider == "linuxserver" for image in linuxserver)

    assert {image.live_view for image in linuxserver} == {"selkies"}


def test_legacy_kasm_images_pin_their_last_published_tag():
    """Kasm stopped shipping current tags for some legacy images.

    The catalog must surface the last tag that actually exists, otherwise the
    card looks selectable but the pull fails with "tag not found".
    """
    images = list_images(provider="kasmweb")
    teams = next(image for image in images if image.repository == "kasmweb/teams")

    assert teams.image == "kasmweb/teams:1.12.0"
    assert "1.12.0" in teams.tags

    query: Optional[str] = None,
    category: Optional[str] = None,
    kind: str = "linux",

) -> List[ComputerImage]:
    """Filter the catalog by provider, free text and category."""
    if kind and kind not in ("linux", "desktop", ""):
        # Windows/macOS images are provided by dockurr, not this library.
        return []
    images = all_catalog_images(provider=provider, refresh=refresh)
    term = (query or "").strip().lower()
    category = (category or "").strip().lower()
    if category:
        images = [image for image in images if image.category.lower() == category]

        ]
    return images

def resolve_image(
    image: Optional[str],
    provider: Optional[str] = None,
    kind: str = "linux",
) -> ImageSpec:
    """
    Resolve an image reference into the Docker/live-view profile.

    Known providers:
      * ``linuxserver/webtop``: Selkies web desktop on 3000 (HTTP, subfolder).
      * ``kasmweb/*``: KasmVNC web desktop on 6901 (HTTPS, strip prefix).
      * anything else: generic container; screenshot/screenshot fallback.

    The Kasm profile is still driven through ``docker exec`` by the X11 agent;
    the HTTPS KasmVNC page is only the human live view.
    """
    raw = (image or "").strip()
    hint = (provider or "").strip().lower()
    if not raw:
        if kind in ("windows", "macos"):
            raw = ""
        elif hint in ("kasmweb", "kasm"):
            raw = _kasm_image("desktop")
        else:
            raw = _linuxserver_image(DEFAULT_LINUXSERVER_TAG)

    lowered = raw.lower()
    if hint in ("kasmweb", "kasm") or lowered.startswith("kasmweb/") or "/kasmweb/" in lowered:
        repository, tag = _split_image(raw)
        repo_name = repository.split("kasmweb/", 1)[-1] if "kasmweb/" in repository else repository
        repository = f"kasmweb/{repo_name}"
        catalog = find_catalog_image(repository)
        # No explicit tag: honour the catalog default, which for legacy images
        # is the last tag Kasm actually published (see _KASM_TAG_OVERRIDES).
        tag = tag or (catalog.default_tag if catalog else DEFAULT_KASM_TAG)
        name = catalog.name if catalog else repo_name.replace("-", " ").title()
        return ImageSpec(
            provider="kasmweb",
            image=f"{repository}:{tag}",
            repository=repository,
            tag=tag,
            live_view="kasmvnc",
            live_port=6901,
            live_scheme="https",
            strip_prefix=True,
            control="docker",
            viewer_user="kasm_user",
            name=name,
            docs_url=KASM_DOCS,
        )

    if hint in ("linuxserver", "lscr") or "linuxserver/webtop" in lowered:
        repository, tag = _split_image(raw)
        tag = tag or DEFAULT_LINUXSERVER_TAG
        catalog = find_catalog_image("linuxserver/webtop", tag)
        return ImageSpec(
            provider="linuxserver",
            image=f"{LINUXSERVER_IMAGE}:{tag}",
            repository="linuxserver/webtop",
            tag=tag,
            live_view="selkies",
            live_port=3000,
            live_scheme="http",
            strip_prefix=False,
            control="docker",
            name=catalog.name if catalog else f"LinuxServer webtop ({tag})",
            docs_url=LS_WEBTOP_DOCS,
        )

    # Unknown image: still run it as a desktop container, but expose only the
    # screenshot fallback until the user picks a known library image.
    repository, tag = _split_image(raw)
    return ImageSpec(
        provider="custom",
        image=raw,
        repository=repository or raw,
        tag=tag or "latest",
        live_view="screenshot",
        live_port=None,
        live_scheme="http",
        strip_prefix=False,
        control="docker",
        name=repository or raw,
        docs_url=None,
    )

    provider: str,
    repository: str,
    refresh: bool = False,
) -> List[ComputerImageTag]:
    """Return selectable tags for a repository (cached, with fallback)."""
    provider = (provider or "").strip().lower()
    repository = (repository or "").strip()
    fallback_tag = DEFAULT_KASM_TAG if provider == "kasmweb" else DEFAULT_LINUXSERVER_TAG
    static = find_catalog_image(repository)
    if static:
        fallback_tag = static.default_tag

    try:
        if provider in ("kasmweb", "kasm"):
            repo = repository if repository.startswith("kasmweb/") else f"kasmweb/{repository}"
            data = _cached_json(
                f"kasmweb:tags:{repo}",
                lambda: _http_json(
                    f"https://hub.docker.com/v2/repositories/{repo}/tags"
                    "?page_size=100&ordering=last_updated"
                ),
                0 if refresh else TAGS_TTL_SECONDS,
            )
            tags = []
            for item in (data or {}).get("results", []):
                name = (item.get("name") or "").strip()
                if not name or name.startswith(("aarch64-", "x86_64-", "arm64v8-")):
                    continue
                tags.append(ComputerImageTag(name=name, updated_at=item.get("last_updated")))
            return _sort_tags(tags) or [ComputerImageTag(name=fallback_tag)]

        if provider in ("linuxserver", "lscr"):
            data = _cached_json(

                lambda: _http_json(

            tags = []
            for item in (data or {}).get("data", {}).get("repositories", {}).get("linuxserver", []):

                    continue
                for tag in item.get("tags") or []:
                    name = (tag.get("tag") or "").strip()
                    # alpine-kde/arch-kde are Wayland-only and do not expose

                    if name and name not in ("dev", "alpine-kde", "arch-kde"):

            return _sort_tags(tags) or [ComputerImageTag(name=fallback_tag)]
    except Exception as ex:
        logger.debug("Could not fetch tags for %s/%s: %s", provider, repository, ex)

request.content:
"""Merged catalog of the image library.

The UI used to read the library from four independent feeds — the provider
catalog (``/computers/images``), the saved computers (``/computers/library``)
and the custom coworking gallery (``/computers/library/custom``) — with three
different item shapes and two different preview mechanisms (public URL versus
authenticated blob).  That is why there was no single grid.

This module flattens the three feeds into ONE list of :class:`CatalogImage` so a
grid can render, search and filter the whole library with one request.  The
custom image keeps its whole manifest nested under ``coworking_image``: the
client reads ``{ coworking_image: { env } }`` (see ``client/src/utils/imageEnv.js``)
and flattening it is what silently empties the create-session form.
"""
from typing import Any, Dict, Iterable, List, Optional

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

#: Sources of the merged feed.  Providers come first so the grid opens on the
#: catalog, then the project's saved computers, then the coworking gallery.
CATALOG_SOURCES = ("linuxserver", "kasmweb", "browseruse", "saved", "custom")


class CatalogImage(BaseModel):
    """One card of the unified image grid."""

    source: str = Field(description="linuxserver, kasmweb, browseruse, saved or custom")
    id: str = Field(description="Stable id inside its source")
    name: str = Field(description="Human readable name")
    description: Optional[str] = Field(default=None, description="Short description")
    type: Optional[str] = Field(default=None, description="Grid type: desktop, application, browser, saved, custom")
    tags: List[str] = Field(default_factory=list, description="Search/filter tags")
    visibility: Optional[str] = Field(default=None, description="user, project, custom or global")
    status: str = Field(default="ready", description="ready, draft or error")
    icon_url: Optional[str] = Field(default=None, description="Icon (public URL when possible)")
    preview_url: Optional[str] = Field(default=None, description="Preview URL when public")
    has_preview_blob: bool = Field(
        default=False,
        description="True when the preview must be fetched from the authenticated blob route",
    )
    image: Optional[str] = Field(default=None, description="Docker image reference")
    provider: Optional[str] = Field(default=None, description="Image provider/profile")
    coworking_image: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Full custom-image manifest (source=custom); keeps `env` nested",
    )


class CatalogImageListResponse(BaseModel):
    """Unified image library response."""

    count: int
    images: List[CatalogImage]


def _provider_type(image: Any) -> str:
    """Grid type of a provider catalog entry."""
    category = (getattr(image, "category", "") or "").strip().lower()
    if not category:
        return "desktop"
    if category.startswith("desktop"):
        return "desktop"
    if "browser" in category or "automation" in category:
        return "browser"
    return "application"


def _provider_items(images: Optional[Iterable[Any]]) -> List[CatalogImage]:
    """Map provider catalog entries (``ComputerImage``) to catalog items."""
    items: List[CatalogImage] = []
    for image in images or []:
        items.append(CatalogImage(
            source=(getattr(image, "provider", "") or "curated"),
            id=image.id,
            name=image.name,
            description=(image.description or None),
            type=_provider_type(image),
            tags=list(image.tags or []),
            visibility="global",
            status="ready",
            icon_url=image.icon_url,
            preview_url=getattr(image, "screenshot_url", None),
            has_preview_blob=False,
            image=image.image,
            provider=image.provider,
        ))
    return items


def _saved_items(computers: Optional[Iterable[Any]]) -> List[CatalogImage]:
    """Map saved computers (``SavedComputer``) to catalog items."""
    items: List[CatalogImage] = []
    for item in computers or []:
        items.append(CatalogImage(
            source="saved",
            id=item.id,
            name=item.name,
            description=getattr(item, "description", None) or None,
            type="saved",
            tags=list(getattr(item, "tags", None) or []),
            visibility=getattr(item, "visibility", None),
            status=getattr(item, "status", None) or "ready",
            icon_url=None,
            # The preview is only served by /computers/library/{id}/preview,
            # behind the API auth: the grid must fetch it as a blob.
            preview_url=None,
            has_preview_blob=bool(getattr(item, "has_preview", False)),
            image=getattr(item, "image", None),
            provider=getattr(item, "provider", None),
        ))
    return items


def _custom_items(images: Optional[Iterable[Any]]) -> List[CatalogImage]:
    """Map coworking gallery entries (``CoworkingImage``) to catalog items."""
    items: List[CatalogImage] = []
    for item in images or []:
        payload = item.to_dict() if hasattr(item, "to_dict") else dict(item)
        items.append(CatalogImage(
            source="custom",
            id=item.id,
            name=item.name,
            description=item.description or None,
            type="custom",
            tags=list(item.tags or []),
            visibility=item.visibility,
            status=item.status or "draft",
            icon_url=item.icon_url,
            # Icon and preview live in the definition folder and are only
            # readable through /computers/library/custom/{id}/media.
            preview_url=None,
            has_preview_blob=bool(item.screenshot_url or item.media),
            image=item.docker_image(),
            provider="custom",
            coworking_image=payload,
        ))
    return items


def build_catalog(
    provider_images: Optional[Iterable[Any]] = None,
    saved_computers: Optional[Iterable[Any]] = None,
    custom_images: Optional[Iterable[Any]] = None,
) -> List[CatalogImage]:
    """Merge the three feeds into one ordered list (pure, no IO)."""
    return [
        *_provider_items(provider_images),
        *_saved_items(saved_computers),
        *_custom_items(custom_images),
    ]


def _matches(item: CatalogImage, needle: str) -> bool:
    haystack = " ".join([
        item.id,
        item.name,
        item.description or "",
        item.image or "",
        item.type or "",
        " ".join(item.tags),
    ]).lower()
    return needle in haystack


def filter_catalog(
    items: Iterable[CatalogImage],
    query: Optional[str] = None,
    type: Optional[str] = None,
    tag: Optional[str] = None,
    visibility: Optional[str] = None,
    status: Optional[str] = None,
    source: Optional[str] = None,
) -> List[CatalogImage]:
    """Apply the grid filters server-side, case-insensitively (pure)."""
    needle = (query or "").strip().lower()
    wanted_type = (type or "").strip().lower()

def _linuxserver_image(tag: str) -> str:
    return f"{LINUXSERVER_IMAGE}:{tag}"


def _linuxserver_entries(with_dynamic: bool = True, refresh: bool = False) -> List[ComputerImage]:
    """Curated webtop flavours, enriched with live tag descriptions."""
    descriptions: Dict[str, str] = {}
    latest: Dict[str, str] = {}
    if with_dynamic:
        try:
            data = _cached_json(
                "linuxserver:webtop",
                lambda: _http_json(
                    "https://api.linuxserver.io/api/v1/images"
                    "?include_config=false&include_deprecated=false"
                ),
                0 if refresh else CACHE_TTL_SECONDS,
            )
            for item in (data or {}).get("data", {}).get("repositories", {}).get("linuxserver", []):
                if item.get("name") != "webtop":
                    continue
                for tag in item.get("tags") or []:
                    name = (tag.get("tag") or "").strip()
                    if name:
                        descriptions[name] = tag.get("desc") or ""
                latest["webtop"] = item.get("version_timestamp") or ""
        except Exception as ex:
            logger.debug("Could not enrich LinuxServer webtop catalog: %s", ex)

    entries = []
    for tag, name, description in _LINUXSERVER_FLAVORS:
        entries.append(ComputerImage(
            id=f"linuxserver:webtop:{tag}",
            provider="linuxserver",
            repository="linuxserver/webtop",
            image=_linuxserver_image(tag),
            tag=tag,
            default_tag=tag,
            name=name,
            description=descriptions.get(tag) or description,
            category="Desktop",
            icon_url=LS_WEBTOP_LOGO,
            screenshot_url=None,
            docs_url=LS_WEBTOP_DOCS,
            updated_at=latest.get("webtop") or None,
            live_view="selkies",
            live_port=3000,
            live_scheme="http",
            strip_prefix=False,
            control="docker",
            tags=[tag, "webtop", "linuxserver", "selkies"],
        ))
    return entries


def _kasm_entries() -> List[ComputerImage]:
    """Curated Kasmweb desktops and applications."""
    entries = []
    for repo, name, description, category in _KASM_DESKTOPS + _KASM_APPS:
        is_desktop = (repo, name, description, category) in _KASM_DESKTOPS
        tag = _KASM_TAG_OVERRIDES.get(repo) or DEFAULT_KASM_TAG
        entries.append(ComputerImage(
            id=f"kasmweb:{repo}:{tag}",
            provider="kasmweb",
            repository=f"kasmweb/{repo}",
            image=_kasm_image(repo, tag),
            tag=tag,
            default_tag=tag,
            name=name,
            description=description,
            category=category,
            icon_url=f"{KASM_SCREENSHOT_BASE}/{repo}.png",
            screenshot_url=f"{KASM_SCREENSHOT_BASE}/{repo}.png",
            docs_url=KASM_DOCS,
            live_view="kasmvnc",
            live_port=6901,
            live_scheme="https",
            strip_prefix=True,
            control="docker",
            viewer_user="kasm_user",
            tags=[repo, tag, "kasmweb", "kasmvnc", "desktop" if is_desktop else "application"],
        ))
    return entries


def _browseruse_entries() -> List[ComputerImage]:
    """Official browser-use images (headless Playwright + Chromium)."""
    return [ComputerImage(
        id=f"browseruse:browseruse:latest",
        provider="browseruse",
        repository="browseruse/browseruse",
        image=f"{BROWSERUSE_IMAGE}:latest",
        tag="latest",
        default_tag="latest",
        name="Browser-Use agent",
        description=(
            "Official browser-use image: Python 3.12, Playwright and Chromium "
            "preinstalled for AI browser automation. Headless: no desktop and "
            "no noVNC, the live view is a screenshot stream."
        ),
        category="Automation",
        docs_url=BROWSERUSE_DOCS,
        live_view="screenshot",
        live_port=None,
        live_scheme="http",
        strip_prefix=False,
        control="docker",
        tags=["browseruse", "browser-use", "browser", "automation", "playwright", "latest"],
    )]


def all_catalog_images(provider: Optional[str] = None, refresh: bool = False) -> List[ComputerImage]:
    """Return the curated catalog, optionally enriched from upstream APIs."""
    provider = (provider or "").strip().lower() or None
    images: List[ComputerImage] = []
    if provider in (None, "all", "linuxserver", "lscr"):
        images.extend(_linuxserver_entries(with_dynamic=True, refresh=refresh))
    if provider in (None, "all", "kasmweb", "kasm"):
        images.extend(_kasm_entries())
    if provider in (None, "all", "browseruse", "browser-use"):
        images.extend(_browseruse_entries())
    return images


def list_images(
    provider: Optional[str] = None,
    query: Optional[str] = None,
    category: Optional[str] = None,
    kind: str = "linux",
    refresh: bool = False,
) -> List[ComputerImage]:
    """Filter the catalog by provider, free text and category."""
    if kind and kind not in ("linux", "desktop", ""):
        # Windows/macOS images are provided by dockurr, not this library.
        return []
    images = all_catalog_images(provider=provider, refresh=refresh)
    term = (query or "").strip().lower()
    category = (category or "").strip().lower()
    if category:
        images = [image for image in images if image.category.lower() == category]
    if term:
        images = [
            image for image in images
            if term in image.name.lower()
            or term in image.repository.lower()
            or term in image.description.lower()
            or term in image.category.lower()
            or any(term in tag.lower() for tag in image.tags)
        ]
    return images


def categories(provider: Optional[str] = None) -> List[str]:
    """List distinct categories for the UI chips."""
    seen: List[str] = []
    for image in all_catalog_images(provider=provider):
        if image.category not in seen:
            seen.append(image.category)
    return seen


def find_catalog_image(repository: str, tag: Optional[str] = None) -> Optional[ComputerImage]:
    """Find a catalog entry by repository (and optionally tag).

    The provider is inferred first so a Kasmweb lookup never waits for the
    LinuxServer API (and vice versa).
    """
    repo = (repository or "").strip().lower()
    if "kasmweb/" in repo:
        provider = "kasmweb"
    elif "webtop" in repo:
        provider = "linuxserver"
    else:
        provider = None
    for image in all_catalog_images(provider=provider):
        if image.repository.lower() == repo or image.repository.lower().endswith("/" + repo):
            if tag is None or image.tag == tag:
                return image
    return None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Resolution
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _split_image(image: str) -> Tuple[str, str]:
    """Split ``repo[:tag]`` (registry-safe; ignores digests)."""
    value = (image or "").strip()
    if "@" in value:
        value = value.split("@", 1)[0]
    last_colon = value.rfind(":")
    slash = value.rfind("/")
    if last_colon > slash:
        return value[:last_colon], value[last_colon + 1:]
    return value, ""


def resolve_image(
    image: Optional[str],
    provider: Optional[str] = None,
    kind: str = "linux",
) -> ImageSpec:
    """
    Resolve an image reference into the Docker/live-view profile.

    Known providers:
      * ``linuxserver/webtop``: Selkies web desktop on 3000 (HTTP, subfolder).
      * ``kasmweb/*``: KasmVNC web desktop on 6901 (HTTPS, strip prefix).
      * anything else: generic container; screenshot/screenshot fallback.

    The Kasm profile is still driven through ``docker exec`` by the X11 agent;
    the HTTPS KasmVNC page is only the human live view.
    """
    raw = (image or "").strip()
    hint = (provider or "").strip().lower()
    if not raw:
        if kind in ("windows", "macos"):
            raw = ""
        elif hint in ("browseruse", "browser-use"):
            raw = f"{BROWSERUSE_IMAGE}:latest"
        elif hint in ("kasmweb", "kasm"):
            raw = _kasm_image("desktop")
        else:
            raw = _linuxserver_image(DEFAULT_LINUXSERVER_TAG)

    lowered = raw.lower()
    if hint in ("browseruse", "browser-use") or lowered.startswith("browseruse/"):
        repository, tag = _split_image(raw)
        repository = repository or BROWSERUSE_IMAGE
        tag = tag or "latest"
        return ImageSpec(
            provider="browseruse",
            image=f"{repository}:{tag}",
            repository=repository,
            tag=tag,
            live_view="screenshot",
            live_port=None,
            live_scheme="http",
            strip_prefix=False,
            control="docker",
            name="Browser-Use agent",
            docs_url=BROWSERUSE_DOCS,
        )

    if hint in ("kasmweb", "kasm") or lowered.startswith("kasmweb/") or "/kasmweb/" in lowered:
        repository, tag = _split_image(raw)
        repo_name = repository.split("kasmweb/", 1)[-1] if "kasmweb/" in repository else repository
        repository = f"kasmweb/{repo_name}"
        catalog = find_catalog_image(repository)
        # No explicit tag: honour the catalog default, which for legacy images
        # is the last tag Kasm actually published (see _KASM_TAG_OVERRIDES).
        tag = tag or (catalog.default_tag if catalog else DEFAULT_KASM_TAG)
        name = catalog.name if catalog else repo_name.replace("-", " ").title()
        return ImageSpec(
            provider="kasmweb",
            image=f"{repository}:{tag}",
            repository=repository,
            tag=tag,
            live_view="kasmvnc",
            live_port=6901,
            live_scheme="https",
            strip_prefix=True,
            control="docker",
            viewer_user="kasm_user",
            name=name,
            docs_url=KASM_DOCS,
        )

    if hint in ("linuxserver", "lscr") or "linuxserver/webtop" in lowered:
        repository, tag = _split_image(raw)
        tag = tag or DEFAULT_LINUXSERVER_TAG
        catalog = find_catalog_image("linuxserver/webtop", tag)
        return ImageSpec(
            provider="linuxserver",
            image=f"{LINUXSERVER_IMAGE}:{tag}",
            repository="linuxserver/webtop",
            tag=tag,
            live_view="selkies",
            live_port=3000,
            live_scheme="http",
            strip_prefix=False,
            control="docker",
            name=catalog.name if catalog else f"LinuxServer webtop ({tag})",
            docs_url=LS_WEBTOP_DOCS,
        )

    # Unknown image: still run it as a desktop container, but expose only the
    # screenshot fallback until the user picks a known library image.
    repository, tag = _split_image(raw)
    return ImageSpec(
        provider="custom",
        image=raw,
        repository=repository or raw,
        tag=tag or "latest",
        live_view="screenshot",
        live_port=None,
        live_scheme="http",
        strip_prefix=False,
        control="docker",
        name=repository or raw,
        docs_url=None,
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tags (live)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def list_image_tags(
    provider: str,
    repository: str,
    refresh: bool = False,
) -> List[ComputerImageTag]:
    """Return selectable tags for a repository (cached, with fallback)."""
    provider = (provider or "").strip().lower()
    repository = (repository or "").strip()
    fallback_tag = DEFAULT_KASM_TAG if provider == "kasmweb" else DEFAULT_LINUXSERVER_TAG
    static = find_catalog_image(repository)
    if static:
        fallback_tag = static.default_tag

    try:
        if provider in ("kasmweb", "kasm"):
            repo = repository if repository.startswith("kasmweb/") else f"kasmweb/{repository}"
            data = _cached_json(
                f"kasmweb:tags:{repo}",
                lambda: _http_json(
                    f"https://hub.docker.com/v2/repositories/{repo}/tags"
                    "?page_size=100&ordering=last_updated"
                ),
                0 if refresh else TAGS_TTL_SECONDS,
            )
            tags = []
            for item in (data or {}).get("results", []):
                name = (item.get("name") or "").strip()
                if not name or name.startswith(("aarch64-", "x86_64-", "arm64v8-")):
                    continue
                tags.append(ComputerImageTag(name=name, updated_at=item.get("last_updated")))
            return _sort_tags(tags) or [ComputerImageTag(name=fallback_tag)]

        if provider in ("linuxserver", "lscr"):
            data = _cached_json(
                "linuxserver:webtop:tags",
                lambda: _http_json(
                    "https://api.linuxserver.io/api/v1/images"
                    "?include_config=false&include_deprecated=false"
                ),
                0 if refresh else TAGS_TTL_SECONDS,
            )
            tags = []
            for item in (data or {}).get("data", {}).get("repositories", {}).get("linuxserver", []):
                if item.get("name") != "webtop":
                    continue
                for tag in item.get("tags") or []:
                    name = (tag.get("tag") or "").strip()
                    # alpine-kde/arch-kde are Wayland-only and do not expose
                    # the X11 display the agent needs.
                    if name and name not in ("dev", "alpine-kde", "arch-kde"):
                        tags.append(ComputerImageTag(name=name, updated_at=item.get("version_timestamp")))
            return _sort_tags(tags) or [ComputerImageTag(name=fallback_tag)]
    except Exception as ex:
        logger.debug("Could not fetch tags for %s/%s: %s", provider, repository, ex)
    return [ComputerImageTag(name=fallback_tag)]


def _sort_tags(tags: Iterable[ComputerImageTag]) -> List[ComputerImageTag]:
    """Stable semantic-ish ordering: stable versions first, then flavors."""
    items = list(tags)
    seen = set()
    unique = []
    for item in items:
        if item.name in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(item.name)
        unique.append(item)
    def rank(item: ComputerImageTag):
        version = re.match(r"^(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)$", item.name)
        if version:
            return (0, tuple(-int(part) for part in version.groups()))
        if re.match(r"^\d+\.\d+\.\d+-rolling-(daily|weekly)$", item.name):
            return (1, item.name)
        return (2, item.name)
    return sorted(unique, key=rank)[:80]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# HTTP cache
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
_CACHE: Dict[str, Tuple[float, Any]] = {}
_CACHE_LOCK = threading.Lock()


def _cached_json(key: str, loader, ttl: int) -> Any:
    """Return a cached JSON response, refreshing after *ttl*."""
    now = time.time()
    with _CACHE_LOCK:
        cached = _CACHE.get(key)
        if cached and now - cached[0] < ttl:
            return cached[1]
    data = loader()
    with _CACHE_LOCK:
        _CACHE[key] = (now, data)
    return data


def _http_json(url: str) -> Any:
    """Fetch a URL as JSON with a short timeout."""
    request = urllib.request.Request(
        url,
        headers={
            "User-Agent": "codx-junior-computer-image-library",
            "Accept": "application/json",
        },
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=10) as response:
        import json
        return json.loads(response.read().decode("utf-8"))

        category="Desktop",

        live_port=3000,
        live_scheme="http",
        tags=["debian-kde", "webtop"],
    )

    return CoworkingImage(
        id="abc123",
        slug="research-desktop",
        name="Research desktop",
        description="KDE with the research toolchain",
        env=[ImageEnvField(name="OPENAI_API_KEY", label="OpenAI key", secret=True)],
        tags=["research", "kde"],

        status="ready",
    )

    return SavedComputer(

        name="My desktop",
        image="codx-library/saved-1:latest",
        created_at="2026-01-01T00:00:00+00:00",
        has_preview=True,
        tags=["saved"],
    )

    assert item.has_preview_blob is False

## What happened

1. Comment carried two asks — **use the official browser-use image** and **fix the image library endpoint** — plus a third: run it through the harness as multiple tasks.
2. The harness could not run: `delegate(2 tasks, wait=true)` returned **`status: failed` on both subagents** with `error: "cannot pickle '_asyncio.Future' object"`. Both workstreams were therefore executed serially, by me.
3. Both asks are now **implemented and tested**: one merged catalog endpoint (`GET /api/computers/images/catalog`) and `browseruse/browseruse` as a first-class catalog entry.
4. Honest gaps, stated up front: the **grid component is still not written** (only the client method that calls the endpoint), and the endpoint is **not live yet** — `codx-junior-api` still runs the 3-hour-old code, and restarting it would kill the backend of this very conversation.

## What I did

**1. The merged endpoint — the thing the comment called "fix the image library endpoint"**

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `api/codx/junior/computer/catalog.py` | **new, 197 lines** — `CatalogImage`, `CatalogImageListResponse`, `build_catalog()`, `filter_catalog()`, all pure/no-IO |
| `api/codx/junior/api/computer.py` | `+77` — `GET /images/catalog` handler |
| `client/src/api/modules/computers.js` | `+21` — `computers.imageCatalog(filters)` |

```
GET /api/computers/images/catalog?provider=&q=&type=&tag=&visibility=&status=&source=&refresh=
→ { count, images: [ { source, id, name, description, type, tags[], visibility,
                       status, icon_url, preview_url, has_preview_blob,
                       image, provider, coworking_image } ] }
```

The handler fans the three feeds out through `asyncio.gather` + `asyncio.to_thread` — `list_images()` (provider catalog), `SavedComputerLibrary.list()` (saved computers), `CoworkingImageLibrary.list_visible()` (coworking gallery) — then merges and applies every filter **server-side**, so the grid needs one request where it used to need four.

The invariant promised in the previous handover is honoured and tested: a custom image keeps its whole manifest **nested under `coworking_image`**, so `client/src/utils/imageEnv.js` still finds `{ coworking_image: { env } }` and the "Image settings" form of `BrowserSessionCreateModal.vue` is untouched. Previews stay honest too: `preview_url` is `null` wherever the real image sits behind auth, and `has_preview_blob` tells the grid to use the blob route (`/library/{id}/preview`, `/library/custom/{id}/media`).

**2. The official browser-use image**

`api/codx/junior/computer/images.py` `+55`: `BROWSERUSE_IMAGE = "browseruse/browseruse"`, a curated provider `browseruse` with the entry `browseruse:browseruse:latest`, wired into `all_catalog_images()` and `resolve_image()`.

I did **not** swap the shared-browser default, and that is a deliberate engineering call, not an omission:

- the shared browser is driven by Playwright **over CDP** and watched through **noVNC**;
- `browseruse/browseruse` is headless — no X display, no CDP port published, no noVNC;
- swapping it would kill both the automation channel and the live screen at once.

So the image is offered in the library with `live_view: "screenshot"` and picked through the existing `CODX_BROWSER_IMAGE`, and the trade-off is documented in a comment next to `DEFAULT_BROWSER_IMAGE` in `docker_browser_manager.py` (`+6`). Also recorded in the catalog description: there is **no official Docker Hub image for the Web UI** — `browser-use/web-ui` is deployed from its docker-compose (7788 UI / 6080 noVNC), while `smanx/browser-use-web-ui`, `vovan/browser-use` and `reqeique/browser-use-api` are community images, not curated defaults.

**3. Validation — the evidence, not a claim**

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `qa_run_tests(paths=["api/tests/computer"])` | **81 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors** (13.8 s) |
| catalog + images tests | **15 passed** |
| route wiring (`import codx.junior.api.computer` → `/images/catalog` registered) | **1 passed** |
| `qa_review_changes` | **294 passed, 0 failed**, coverage **100.0 %** — verdict `require_approval`, see below |
| `security_review_changes` | **allow**, risk 0, 0 findings |

The `require_approval` verdict is **not** from this change: it is the 11 pre-existing `change.missing-tests` findings on an already-dirty tree (102 changed files, e.g. `db.py`, `tasks.py`, `browser_manager.py`), none of which I touched. My diff: 9 files, +613/-5, of which `test_coworking_background.py` (+117) was already untracked before this turn.

**4. Not done, stated plainly** — no grid component, no api restart, no harness (see Next tasks). Nothing here is claimed as working that a test has not shown.

## Demo

One command, the real gate over the whole computer suite:

```
qa_run_tests(paths=["api/tests/computer"], suite="pytest:api")   →   81 passed, 0 failed
```

## Next tasks

- `quick` — Restart `codx-junior-api` and smoke the new route (`GET /api/computers/images/catalog?q=kasm&source=kasmweb`). Deferred on purpose: restarting that container kills the backend of the running conversation.
- `max` — The grid itself: one component consuming `computers.imageCatalog(filters)`, replacing the four loaders (`images`, `images/tags`, `library`, `library/custom`), with the blob preview path when `has_preview_blob` is true.
- `quick` — Harness: `delegate` dies with `cannot pickle '_asyncio.Future' object` on every subagent, so "one task, several workstreams" is impossible today; fix it or route that pattern through `orchestrator`.
- `quick` — Still open from before, untouched: desktop X11 (`computer_*` containers stuck in `Created`, `Can't open display: (null)`), the atlas (21 files indexed), and `client/tmp-vue-sfc-check.mjs`.

```py api/codx/junior/ai/smol/parallel.py
"""
Execution scheduling for SmolAgent tool rounds.

One model round routinely asks for several tools at once: read three files,
search the atlas, fetch a page. Executing them one after the other pays the SUM
of their latencies, and a harness turn can issue dozens of calls (up to
``max_tool_calls`` per round, many rounds).

Executing the whole round at once is not safe either: some tools mutate shared
state (the working tree, the git index, the kanban board, the shared browser
page, one Docker daemon) and their order matters.

This module decides, per call, whether it may run CONCURRENTLY with its
neighbours and groups an ordered round into batches::

    round  : [read_a, read_b, read_c, write_x, read_a2]
    batches: [[read_a, read_b, read_c], [write_x], [read_a2]]

Batches always run in order and the calls inside a batch run concurrently, so
the model's call order is preserved exactly — a call never observes the state
from before a preceding call — while the common case (a burst of independent
reads, all I/O bound: files, HTTP, git/docker CLI) costs the latency of its
slowest call instead of the sum.

Classification rules, in priority order:

1. ``ToolSettings.parallel`` set on the tool registry entry (``True`` forces
   concurrent execution, ``False`` forces a barrier).
2. Registry ``tags`` that mark a mutation (``write``, ``modification``,
   ``deletion``, ``destructive``, ``creation``).
3. The explicit name list and tokens below (stateful tools, shared interactive
   sessions, heavy subprocess runs).
4. Everything else runs concurrently: an unknown tool is far more likely to be
   a read than a mutation.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior

        self,
        chat: Any,
        *,
        parent_token: Any = None,

        """
        Execute a one-off delegated subagent card (``delegate`` tool).

        Args:
            chat: The delegated chat, containing the delegate contract.
            parent_token: Optional parent cancellation token.
            timeout: Optional timeout (defaults to the step timeout).
        """
        started = time.monotonic()
        cost_before = self._cost_of(chat)
        error = ""
        try:
            await self.run_chat(
                chat,
                system=STEP_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
                timeout=timeout or C.DEFAULT_STEP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
                parent_token=parent_token,
            )
        except StepTimeout as ex:
            error = str(ex)
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            raise
        except Exception as ex:
            logger.exception(
                "Orchestration: delegated task failed for chat '%s': %s",
                getattr(chat, "id", ""),
                ex,
            )
            error = str(ex)

        duration = time.monotonic() - started
        cost = max(0.0, self._cost_of(chat) - cost_before)
        message = self._last_assistant_message(chat)
        content = str(getattr(message, "content", "") or "") if message else ""
        error = error or self._message_error(chat)
        result = parse_step_result(
            content,
            error=error or None,
            cost_cxjcoins=cost,
            duration_seconds=duration,
        )
        return self._downgrade_on_tool_limit(

async def delegate(
    task: Optional[str] = None,
    tasks: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    profile: Optional[str] = None,
    files: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    board: Optional[str] = None,
    column: Optional[str] = None,
    concurrency: Optional[int] = None,
    wait: bool = True,
    context: Optional[str] = None,
    timeout_seconds: Optional[int] = None,
    settings: Any = None,
    session: Any = None,
) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    Execute a ``delegate`` call: isolated subagents as visible task cards.

    Args:
        task/tasks: One task or a list of self-contained tasks.
        profile: Optional profile for the subagents.
        files: Relevant files.
        board/column: Card destination.
        concurrency: Max simultaneous subagents.
        wait: Wait for results (True) or create a durable run (False).
        context: Extra context for every contract.
        timeout_seconds: Per-subagent timeout.
    """
    if settings is None:
        raise ValueError("delegate requires project settings")
    chat = _current_chat(session=session, settings=settings)
    service = _service(settings, session)

    clean_tasks: List[str] = []
    if task and str(task).strip():
        clean_tasks.append(str(task).strip())
    for item in tasks or []:
        text = str(item or "").strip()
        if text:
            clean_tasks.append(text)
    if not clean_tasks:
        raise ValueError("delegate requires 'task' or 'tasks'")

    outcome = await service.delegate(
        chat,
        clean_tasks,
        profile=(profile or "").lstrip("@"),
        files=files,
        board=board,
        column=column,
        concurrency=int(concurrency or 2),
        wait=bool(wait),
        context=context or "",
        timeout=float(timeout_seconds) if timeout_seconds else None,
    )

    if outcome.get("mode") == "run":
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=(
                "🚀 Delegation queued as a durable run "
                f"`{outcome.get('run_id')}`. The cards and the sprint are on the board; "
                "the background worker will execute the tasks."
            ),
            llm_response=_json(outcome),
        )

    results = outcome.get("results") or []
    lines = [f"### Delegation finished ({len(results)} task(s))", ""]
    for index, result in enumerate(results, start=1):
        lines.append(
            f"{index}. **{result.get('status')}** — {result.get('summary')}"
            + (f" (card `{result.get('chat_id')}`)" if result.get("chat_id") else "")
        )
        if result.get("verification"):
            lines.append(f"   - verification: {result['verification']}")
    return ToolResponse(
        user_response="\n".join(lines),
        llm_response=_json(outcome),
    )

## What happened

1. Comment carried two asks — **use the official browser-use image** and **fix the image library endpoint** — plus a third: run it through the harness as multiple tasks.
2. The harness could not run: `delegate(2 tasks, wait=true)` returned **`status: failed` on both subagents** with `error: "cannot pickle '_asyncio.Future' object"`. Both workstreams were therefore executed serially, by me.

4. New comment (`max`): fix `delegate`, fix the grid component build, restart the `api` and `client` containers. This turn established **where the delegate bug is not**, restarted `client`, and deliberately did not restart `api` mid-turn (it is the backend serving this conversation).

## What I did

**1. The merged endpoint — the thing the comment called "fix the image library endpoint"**

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `api/codx/junior/computer/catalog.py` | **new, 197 lines** — `CatalogImage`, `CatalogImageListResponse`, `build_catalog()`, `filter_catalog()`, all pure/no-IO |

```
GET /api/computers/images/catalog?provider=&q=&type=&tag=&visibility=&status=&source=&refresh=
→ { count, images: [ { source, id, name, description, type, tags[], visibility,
                       status, icon_url, preview_url, has_preview_blob,
                       image, provider, coworking_image } ] }
```

The handler fans the three feeds out through `asyncio.gather` + `asyncio.to_thread` — `list_images()` (provider catalog), `SavedComputerLibrary.list()` (saved computers), `CoworkingImageLibrary.list_visible()` (coworking gallery) — then merges and applies every filter **server-side**, so the grid needs one request where it used to need four.

The invariant promised in the previous handover is honoured and tested: a custom image keeps its whole manifest **nested under `coworking_image`**, so `client/src/utils/imageEnv.js` still finds `{ coworking_image: { env } }` and the "Image settings" form of `BrowserSessionCreateModal.vue` is untouched. Previews stay honest too: `preview_url` is `null` wherever the real image sits behind auth, and `has_preview_blob` tells the grid to use the blob route (`/library/{id}/preview`, `/library/custom/{id}/media`).

**2. The official browser-use image**

`api/codx/junior/computer/images.py` `+55`: `BROWSERUSE_IMAGE = "browseruse/browseruse"`, a curated provider `browseruse` with the entry `browseruse:browseruse:latest`, wired into `all_catalog_images()` and `resolve_image()`.

I did **not** swap the shared-browser default, and that is a deliberate engineering call, not an omission:

- the shared browser is driven by Playwright **over CDP** and watched through **noVNC**;
- `browseruse/browseruse` is headless — no X display, no CDP port published, no noVNC;
- swapping it would kill both the automation channel and the live screen at once.

So the image is offered in the library with `live_view: "screenshot"` and picked through the existing `CODX_BROWSER_IMAGE`, and the trade-off is documented in a comment next to `DEFAULT_BROWSER_IMAGE` in `docker_browser_manager.py` (`+6`). Also recorded in the catalog description: there is **no official Docker Hub image for the Web UI** — `browser-use/web-ui` is deployed from its docker-compose (7788 UI / 6080 noVNC), while `smanx/browser-use-web-ui`, `vovan/browser-use` and `reqeique/browser-use-api` are community images, not curated defaults.

| `security_review_changes` | **allow**, risk 0, 0 findings |

The `require_approval` verdict is **not** from this change: it is the 11 pre-existing `change.missing-tests` findings on an already-dirty tree (102 changed files, e.g. `db.py`, `tasks.py`, `browser_manager.py`), none of which I touched. My diff: 9 files, +613/-5, of which `test_coworking_background.py` (+117) was already untracked before this turn.

## This turn — the three `max` asks, stated without decoration

**a) `delegate` — narrowed, not fixed.** Reading the real path
`orchestration_tools.delegate → OrchestrationService.delegate → board.create_delegate_card → executor.execute_delegate → run_chat`:

- **Confirmed:** the harness source does **not** pickle anything. `grep -rln pickle api/codx/junior` returns exactly one file, `security/ciso/malicious.py` (plus its `__pycache__`). That traceback names the library and the line, and it is the one command that closes this bug.

**b) Grid component — not written.** `computers.imageCatalog(filters)` exists and is the only half of the pair; no Vue component consumes it yet. Writing one that compiles means touching the existing computers view, so it is its own increment, not a tail-end addition to this one.

Note that both containers run **built images** — a restart reuses the image, so shipping the new endpoint needs a **build** (`docker_compose_service action=build service=api|client`), not a restart.

## The delegate bug — root cause found and fixed

**The chain, all of it in this repository:**

1. `api/codx/junior/ai/smol/smol_agent.py:1569-1574` — during a turn the agent stashes runtime state **on the settings object**:
   `self.settings._active_session = self.session` and `self.settings._active_cancellation_token = cancellation_token`. The `CancellationToken` (`ai/cancellation.py:16`) owns a live `asyncio.Event`; the session owns live futures.
2. `api/codx/junior/task_workspace.py:515` `settings_for()` — called by `executor._call_engine()` for **every** delegated card and every run step — clones the settings into the worktree scope: `source.model_copy(deep=True)`, falling back to `copy.deepcopy(source)`.
3. Deep-copying the settings therefore means deep-copying live asyncio state → **`TypeError: cannot pickle '_asyncio.Future' object`**, raised in `execute_delegate`'s `except Exception`, logged, and returned as `error` on both cards.

That is exactly why **both subagents failed instantly and identically**: the workspace clone happens *before* the first model call, and a normal (non-delegated) chat never clones the settings — so ordinary turns were unaffected while every delegated card and every orchestrated run step died on its first turn.

**Proof of the mechanism inside the running container** (throwaway probe `api/tmp_attr_check.py`, run with `/home/codx-junior/codx-junior/api/.venv/bin/python`; the QA exec gate refuses `rm`, so the file is still on disk and listed under Next tasks):

```
pydantic: 2.13.5
_active_session -> SETTABLE on CODXJuniorSettings
_active_cancellation_token -> SETTABLE on CODXJuniorSettings
deepcopy of live turn state -> FAILED: TypeError cannot pickle '_contextvars.Context' object
```

Both attributes really do land on the pydantic model, and deep-copying them really does explode — the message names whichever live asyncio object the copy reaches first (`'_contextvars.Context'` in the probe, `'_asyncio.Future'` in the failing delegated turn).

**The fix** — `api/codx/junior/task_workspace.py`:

```python
RUNTIME_SETTINGS_ATTRS = ("_active_cancellation_token", "_active_session")
```

`settings_for()` now detaches those two attributes from the source settings, clones, and restores them in a `finally`. The clone never inherits another turn's live state (the worker installs its own), the parent keeps its token (so `delegate` still cancels its subagents), and the worktree clone is unchanged in every other respect.

**Regression test** — `api/tests/test_task_workspace.py::test_settings_clone_ignores_live_turn_state`: a stand-in token holding a **real `asyncio.Future`** plus a session object are attached to the settings; `settings_for()` must return a clone, the clone must not carry them, and the parent must still hold them. It fails on the old code with the production error and passes now.

    # Runtime-only attributes the agent runtime attaches to the settings object
    # for the span of a turn. They hold live asyncio objects (the cancellation
    # token owns an ``asyncio.Event``) and a session, none of which survive a
    # deep copy: cloning them raises ``cannot pickle '_asyncio.Future' object``
    # and kills the first turn of every delegated card / run step.
    RUNTIME_SETTINGS_ATTRS = ("_active_cancellation_token", "_active_session")

    def _detach_runtime_attrs(self, source: Any) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Remove the runtime-only attributes so *source* can be deep-copied."""
        detached: Dict[str, Any] = {}
        for attr in self.RUNTIME_SETTINGS_ATTRS:
            try:
                if hasattr(source, attr):
                    detached[attr] = getattr(source, attr)
                    delattr(source, attr)
            except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
                continue
        return detached

    def _reattach_runtime_attrs(self, source: Any, detached: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        for attr, value in detached.items():
            try:
                setattr(source, attr, value)
            except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
                pass
```

class CancellationToken:
    """
    A token that can be used to cancel an in-flight AI request.

    Each token carries a unique ``token_id`` (UUID4) that is sent to clients
    via the response message metadata so they can cancel the request either by
    ``chat_id`` or by ``token_id``.

    flowchart TD
        A[Create token] --> B[Assign token_id UUID]
        B --> C{cancel() called?}
        C -->|Yes| D[Set cancelled_at timestamp]
        D --> E[Raise CancelledError on next check]
        C -->|No| F[Request completes normally]
    """

    def __init__(self, chat_id: str) -> None:
        self.chat_id: str = chat_id
        self.token_id: str = str(uuid.uuid4())
        self.cancelled_at: Optional[datetime] = None
        self._event = asyncio.Event()
        # Abort hooks run when the token is cancelled: the agent registers one
        # to close the in-flight provider stream, which is what makes "stop"
        # immediate instead of waiting for the next chunk (or the whole model
        # round) to arrive.
        self._callbacks: List[Callable[[], None]] = []
        self._callbacks_lock = threading.Lock()

    @property
    def is_cancelled(self) -> bool:
        return self.cancelled_at is not None

    def add_callback(self, callback: Callable[[], None]) -> None:
        """Run *callback* on cancellation (immediately when already cancelled)."""
        if not callable(callback):
            return
        run_now = False
        with self._callbacks_lock:
            if self.is_cancelled:
                run_now = True
            else:
                self._callbacks.append(callback)
        if run_now:
            self._run_callback(callback)

    @staticmethod
    def _run_callback(callback: Callable[[], None]) -> None:
        """Invoke one abort hook, never letting it break cancellation."""
        try:
            callback()
        except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - abort hooks are best effort
            logger.exception("CancellationToken callback failed")

    def cancel(self) -> None:
        """Mark this token as cancelled and run every abort hook."""

"""Per-task git workspaces: isolated checkouts for autonomous agent work.

The problem this module solves is not git: it is *ownership*. An autonomous
agent that writes into the main checkout mixes its changes with every other
task, with the human's edits and with runtime state. By the time a reviewer
looks at `git status`, the diff is a single pile and no commit can be attributed
to the work that produced it.

Each task tree (a chat and its descendants, identified by ``root_id``) gets:

* a dedicated branch ``codx/task/<slug>-<hash>`` cut from the current branch,
* a git worktree under ``<git_worktrees_path>/tasks/<slug>-<hash>``,
* a registry entry in the project data plane (``.codx/task_workspaces``).

An autonomous turn runs with a *clone* of the project settings whose
``abs_project_path`` is the worktree, so every file and git tool sees the
isolated checkout. The main checkout stays exactly as it was. At the end of the
turn the workspace is committed on its branch, which is what the Git view
reviews, merges or discards. The clone keeps ``codx_path`` untouched: chats,
task cards, settings and the audit journal stay in the project.

Safety rules:
    * Disabled by ``task_workspace_isolation=False`` (settings) or a non-git
      project: the caller falls back to the main checkout.
    * A workspace is never created for a chat that already has one; the same
      task keeps its branch across turns.

      gitignored env files are copied so the agent has the same runtime
      configuration. Nothing is copied that git would track.
    * Commits never use ``--no-verify``: the CISO pre-commit gate still runs.
    * Registry writes are atomic and guarded by a cross-process lock, so several

def _utcnow() -> str:
    """Return the current UTC timestamp as ISO-8601."""
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()


def _slug(value: Any, limit: int = 40) -> str:
    """Return a filesystem/branch safe slug of *value*."""
    text = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]+", "-", str(value or "task")).strip("-._")
    text = text or "task"
    return text[:limit].strip("-._") or "task"


def _hash(value: str) -> str:
    """Return a short stable hash used to keep workspace names unique."""
    return hashlib.sha1(str(value or "").encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:8]


def _run_git(cwd: str, args: List[str], timeout: int = GIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) -> tuple:
    """Run git in *cwd* without a shell.

    Returns:
        tuple: ``(ok, stdout, stderr)``.
    """
    command = ["git", "--no-pager", "-c", "core.quotepath=false", *args]
    try:
        completed = subprocess.run(
            command,
            cwd=cwd,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=timeout,
        )
    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as ex:
        return False, "", str(ex)
    return completed.returncode == 0, completed.stdout, completed.stderr


def _git_ok(cwd: str, args: List[str]) -> bool:
    """Return True when a quiet git command succeeds."""
    ok, _stdout, _stderr = _run_git(cwd, args)
    return ok
